quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What should you do when taking a long trip?

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel tired.
Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold weather.
Ride more than 12 hours per day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold weather.
questions.explanation: To prevent fatigue on a long trip, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take breaks at least every two hours. Do not use stimulants like caffeine. They cause extreme tiredness when they wear off.

questions.question: How can you stop other drivers from sharing your lane?

options.text: Make angry gestures at other drivers.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane leaves less space on both sides of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for other drivers to share your lane.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front of the group. This lets experienced riders watch them from the back.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect a rider's ability to ride safely?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride. Riding while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to let them pass.
Speed up to create distance between you.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If you can do it safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make them follow you faster and increase danger.

questions.question: Why should you use your mirrors when stopped at an intersection?

options.text: To see if parked cars are entering traffic.
To see if other vehicles are changing lanes.
To check for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
To see if someone will turn behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
questions.explanation: When stopped at an intersection, use your mirrors to watch for cars approaching from behind. Drivers may not see you in time, so you need to be ready to react.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate during a wobble—it will make your motorcycle more unstable. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly and slow down by gradually closing the throttle. Shift your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not brake, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: What should you focus on when adjusting your mirrors?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the side lane as possible. Your mirror may show a bit of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: How can you stop another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Swerve side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to share it.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should position themselves toward the front of the group, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without forcing the inexperienced rider to lead.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should travel:

options.text: Slower than you would during the day in the same conditions.
At the same speed you would during the day in the same conditions.
Faster than you would during the day in the same conditions.
On the shoulder of the road so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than you would during the day in the same conditions.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than during the day when conditions are the same. It is harder to see hazards in the dark. Slowing down helps you avoid accidents.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation normally. But switch to single-file when going through curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: A wobble, or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars, may be caused by:

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure.
questions.explanation: Most wobbles happen because of improper loading, bad accessories, or wrong tire pressure.

questions.question: If you need to brake while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you are out of the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle leans than when it is upright. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake in a curve, apply the brakes more smoothly and gently than on a straight road.

questions.question: When riding at night, how should your following distance compare to daytime riding?

options.text: Allow a longer following distance at night.
Allow a shorter following distance at night.
Always maintain the same following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distance in the dark because you cannot see shadows and light contrasts. Allow more following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle:

options.text: Allows the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated.
Has a seat even with the rider's waist.
Has a seat that is 10 inches above the rider's waist.
Has a seat that is 10 inches below the rider's waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated.
questions.explanation: A properly-fitted motorcycle lets you touch the ground with your feet while you sit on the seat. When riding, keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: Which of the following best protects your eyes from wind?
questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Most windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Move their shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by releasing the throttle and using both brakes if needed.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: Passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets. Passengers should avoid loose clothing that might catch on the motorcycle and should lean with the operator when turning. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone drinks 7 drinks in 3 hours, how many drinks remain in their system 3 hours after their last drink?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Someone who drank 7 drinks in 3 hours would have about 4 drinks left in their system 3 hours later.

questions.question: When securing a load on a motorcycle, where should you place it?
questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and balanced on both sides. Placing loads high raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance. Uneven loads pull the bike to one side.

questions.question: What lights should you use when riding in fog?

options.text: Both high and low beams alternating

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlight
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is turning off the engine to slow down
It is slowing down by downshifting

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by downshifting
questions.explanation: Engine braking is downshifting to a lower gear to slow down. This works like applying the brakes.
